launcher_layout.operational_implication: There is no separate launcher process. node executes cli.js directly via the shebang. Therefore arch-prop-2's drift check has exactly two viable homes: (a) inside cli.js itself, run synchronously before MCP transport.connect; or (b) introduce a NEW shell wrapper at /usr/local/bin/rednote-mcp (or rename the symlink) that runs the check and then exec's node. Option (a) keeps the install-path single-source; option (b) requires a sysadmin-managed file outside the rednote-mcp tree. We prescribe (a).

issues.title: arch-prop-2 — launch-time drift check: place the check INSIDE dist/cli.js (not a separate wrapper); fail-closed; one-restart-cycle latency
issues.description: The check must live IN the cli.js module loaded by node — not in a sibling shell wrapper. Reason: /usr/bin/rednote-mcp is a direct symlink to dist/cli.js (no shell wrapper exists, and adding one means a sysadmin-managed file outside /root/rednote-mcp, which contradicts the single-source-of-truth invariant). Putting the check in cli.js means the source repo continues to own its own integrity invariant; adding a wrapper would move that ownership outside the repo where it is unaudited and easy to forget. Implementation surface and behavior are PRESCRIBED below; BA can convert these to ACs verbatim.
issues.location: PRIMARY: /root/rednote-mcp/dist/cli.js (new top-of-file block + new helper module dist/utils/deployStampCheck.js). PROPAGATES via deploy-to-usrlib.sh to /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/dist/. SUPPORTING: /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh (must be extended to write the .deploy-stamp file).
issues.runtime_evidence: Prior cycle measured 21598-byte unaccounted drift in installed dist/tools/rednoteTools.js. With this check in place, that exact incident shape is detected at MCP startup of the very next launch.
issues.observation_notes: Concrete prescription follows in implementation_prescription field below. The check is pure file I/O + crypto.createHash; node-builtin only; zero new npm deps.

where_does_the_check_live.answer: INSIDE cli.js, NOT in a wrapper.
where_does_the_check_live.exact_insertion_point: /root/rednote-mcp/dist/cli.js — after the require() block (after line 46 'const execAsync = ...') and BEFORE 'const name = ...' (line 47). Equivalent to running before any McpServer or RedNoteTools is constructed.
where_does_the_check_live.form: Synchronous call to a new helper require('./utils/deployStampCheck').enforceAtLaunch(__dirname). Synchronous because we must NOT begin the McpServer constructor before drift is ruled out — async would let the server start and accept stdio frames during the verification window, which defeats the gate.
where_does_the_check_live.applies_to_all_modes: The check must run for both `--stdio` mode (line 178) AND the commander-driven CLI commands (init, pack-logs, open-logs). All four invocations load the same dist/. Place the call ABOVE the if/else split so it runs unconditionally.
where_does_the_check_live.do_not_add_a_shell_wrapper: Rejected alternatives: (a) /usr/local/bin/rednote-mcp shell wrapper that exec's node — moves the integrity gate outside the repo, sysadmin-managed, easy to skip. (b) systemd ExecStartPre — requires systemd unit, but rednote-mcp is launched on-demand via stdio by an MCP client, not as a daemon. Neither alternative survives the single-source-of-truth invariant from MIGRATION-20260503.md.

deploy_stamp_format.kind: JSON file (not binary, not env file — JSON so the launch-time check uses JSON.parse, no parser dep)

schema.source_path: absolute path of the source dist/ that was rsync'd, e.g. '/root/rednote-mcp/dist'
schema.source_commit_sha: output of `git -C /root/rednote-mcp rev-parse HEAD`, or the literal string 'NOT_A_GIT_WORKING_TREE' if git rev-parse fails (don't crash deploy on non-git source)
schema.source_commit_dirty: boolean — true if `git -C /root/rednote-mcp diff --quiet` exits non-zero, else false
schema.package_version: value of package.json .version at deploy time
schema.files_count: integer — equal to length of files keys; sanity check
schema.manifest_sha256: sha256 of dist/.stealth-applied-fragments at deploy time (single canonical snapshot of the audit trail)

rationale_per_field.schema_version: Forward-compat — a future extension can require schema_version >= 2 and gracefully degrade.
rationale_per_field.source_commit_sha: Lets a human operator do `git log <sha>..HEAD` in /root/rednote-mcp to see what edits exist in source but were not deployed. Not gating because legitimate workflow allows source ahead of installed (the human is editing right now).
rationale_per_field.source_commit_dirty: Same — informational. A dirty deploy is allowed but flagged.
rationale_per_field.package_version: Cross-checked against package.json at launch (in the installed tree). Mismatch is gating — implies someone edited package.json post-deploy.
rationale_per_field.files: THIS is the gating field. Per-file sha256. Launch-time check recomputes sha256 of every actual file under installed dist/ and compares against this map. ANY missing file, ANY extra file, ANY hash mismatch = drift = refuse to launch.
rationale_per_field.files_count: Sanity check against files map size; lets the check fail fast if the JSON parsed but is malformed.
rationale_per_field.manifest_sha256: Single hash of the audit-trail file. Equivalent to having .stealth-applied-fragments in the files map (which it already is); this is a redundant cross-check that surfaces 'someone edited the manifest' specifically in the error message instead of in a long file diff.

what_is_in_the_files_map_exactly.rule: Every regular file under dist/ that the rsync deploy copies. Recursive. Relative paths from dist/ root. Forward slashes regardless of OS. Sorted by key for deterministic JSON output (sort_keys=True semantics).
explicit_inclusions: .deploy-stamp's parent contents EXCEPT .deploy-stamp itself (chicken-and-egg — the stamp cannot list its own hash; see exclusions). dist/cli.js, dist/index.js, dist/auth/authManager.js, dist/tools/rednoteTools.js, dist/utils/deployStampCheck.js (new), dist/utils/logger.js, dist/utils/stdioLogger.js, dist/.stealth-applied-fragments, dist/auth/cookies.json (if present — see exception), and any .d.ts files rsync carried along.
exclusions: .deploy-stamp itself (the stamp does not list its own hash; instead the launch-time check ensures the stamp's parse is structurally valid). Any path matching dist/auth/cookies.json — cookies are mutated at runtime by AuthManager during login, so including them in the gating set would cause every post-login restart to fail. Any *.log file under dist/ (none exist today, but exclude the pattern defensively). The dist/.deploy-stamp file is itself authored by the deploy script after the manifest is computed.
what_is_in_the_files_map_exactly.tooling: Computed via the same `find $TARGET_DIR -type f -exec sha256sum {} \;` that step d of deploy-to-usrlib.sh already runs — extend that step to produce the JSON map instead of throwing the result away after the diff.

failure_mode.rationale: The 2026-04-04 happy-server precedent (and prior cycle's arch-7) classify silent-degradation as the worst outcome — by the time anyone notices, xhs has fast-banned the IP. Refusing to start gives the operator an immediate, loud signal at the next MCP client connect attempt. The MCP client will surface the failure as 'rednote-mcp not responding' which is impossible to ignore.
failure_mode.exit_code: exit 78 (sysexits.h EX_CONFIG = 'configuration error'). Documented, distinguishable from exit 1 (generic).
failure_mode.stderr_message: Multi-line, machine-parseable: first line `[deployStampCheck] FAIL: drift detected vs /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/dist/.deploy-stamp`. Subsequent lines list each mismatched file with `<relpath>  expected=<sha256>  actual=<sha256>`. Final line: `Refusing to start. Re-run /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh from source repo, or restore the installed tree from a known-good snapshot.`
failure_mode.do_not_log_to_stdout: MCP transport is stdio. Writing the failure to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC frame stream. All check output goes to stderr ONLY.
failure_mode.cookies_or_proxy_env_missing_is_NOT_a_dr: Those are runtime concerns (T0'-1, T0'-4 in MIGRATION-20260503.md). The drift check ONLY checks the dist/ filesystem against the .deploy-stamp.

stamp_writer.when: After step e (sha256 round-trip verification passes) and BEFORE exit 0.
new_step_f_pseudocode: 1. Build a JSON document conforming to the schema above.
2. files map = the same per-file sha256 set produced by step d, EXCLUDING .deploy-stamp itself and EXCLUDING dist/auth/cookies.json (use a grep -v filter).
4. source_commit_dirty = `git -C /root/rednote-mcp diff --quiet 2>/dev/null && echo false || echo true`.
7. Write JSON to a temp file then `mv -f` into place at $TARGET_DIR/.deploy-stamp (atomic publish).
8. Print `[deploy-to-usrlib] step f: wrote .deploy-stamp (N files, source_commit=<sha>, dirty=<bool>)`.
stamp_writer.why_atomic_mv: If deploy is interrupted between writing the stamp and the rsync's rename of a file, the stamp could reference a hash that doesn't yet exist on disk, causing the very first launch after a partial deploy to fail. Atomic mv-into-place reduces the window to a single inode rename.

launcher_side_check_pseudocode.module: /root/rednote-mcp/dist/utils/deployStampCheck.js (new) — exports `enforceAtLaunch(distRoot)` and is itself listed in the .deploy-stamp's files map (so a tampered check module is detected by the OTHER files' hashes — circular self-trust is acceptable here because anyone who can edit deployStampCheck.js can also edit cli.js).
behavior: 2. If !fs.existsSync(stampPath): write to stderr 'No .deploy-stamp present at <path>. This installation was not deployed via scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh. Refusing to start.' and process.exit(78). [Bootstrap-friendly variant: see 'bootstrap_problem' field below.]
3. let stamp; try { stamp = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(stampPath, 'utf-8')); } catch (e) { stderr 'Deploy stamp at <path> is not valid JSON: <e.message>. Refusing.' exit(78). }
4. if (stamp.schema_version !== 1) { stderr 'Unsupported deploy-stamp schema_version=<x>; this rednote-mcp expects 1.' exit(78). }
5. const installedPkg = require(path.join(distRoot, '..', 'package.json')); if (installedPkg.version !== stamp.package_version) { stderr ... exit(78). }

6. For each [relpath, expectedHash] in stamp.files: const abs = path.join(distRoot, relpath); if (!fs.existsSync(abs)) record missing(relpath); else const actual = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(abs)).digest('hex'); if (actual !== expectedHash) record mismatch(relpath, expectedHash, actual).
7. Walk distRoot recursively; for each regular file whose relpath is NOT in stamp.files AND is NOT excluded (.deploy-stamp, auth/cookies.json, *.log) record extra(relpath).
8. If missing/mismatch/extra all empty: return (the void return is the success signal). Else: write the multi-line FAIL message to stderr (per failure_mode.stderr_message above) and process.exit(78).

9. Optional: if (stamp.files['.stealth-applied-fragments'] is set AND its hash matches the file AND stamp.manifest_sha256 differs from that hash) emit a warning to stderr ('manifest_sha256 mismatch with files entry — likely stale stamp'). Non-fatal; informational because file-hash gate already covers correctness.
launcher_side_check_pseudocode.imports_used: Only node builtins: fs, path, crypto. No external dep. Compatible with engines.node >=16.
launcher_side_check_pseudocode.performance_budget: On a dist/ tree of ~30 files totaling <1MB, the full sha256 sweep completes in <50ms on a 16-core Hetzner box. This is invisible to MCP startup latency (server.connect alone takes 100-500ms over stdio handshake).

ordering_hazard_analysis.first_launch_after_initial_install_with_: Hazard: on a brand-new host with no prior deploy, the stamp file does not exist and the check refuses to start — bootstrap deadlock. Mitigation: the deploy script writes the stamp (step f). On a fresh host, the operator's first action per MIGRATION-20260503.md T0'-5 is to run scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh. That run creates the stamp. THEREFORE the bootstrap path is: (1) clone /root/rednote-mcp, (2) `npm install` in source repo (allowed by the preinstall guard because preinstall is set BY arch-prop-3, see ordering_hazard below), (3) ensure /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/ exists (operator may copy or `npm pack && npm install -g` — see arch-prop-3 prescription), (4) run scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh which writes the stamp, (5) start MCP. Step 4 is mandatory before step 5. This is documented in the README banner from arch-prop-3.
ordering_hazard_analysis.stamp_predates_drift_check_module_itself: Hazard: the very first deploy that ships deployStampCheck.js writes a stamp listing deployStampCheck.js's hash. cli.js then tries to require('./utils/deployStampCheck'). Subsequent launches: stamp lists deployStampCheck.js hash, check passes. No deadlock. The CIRCULAR self-trust (the gate verifies the gate) is acceptable: an attacker who can rewrite deployStampCheck.js to no-op the check could equally rewrite cli.js to skip calling it — both paths require write to /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/dist/, which is the very thing the launch-time check is designed to detect AT NEXT START. The check trades 'detects edits between deploys' for 'cannot detect an edit that ALSO updated the stamp', which only a fully sanctioned deploy run can do — by definition, sanctioned deploys are not drift.
ordering_hazard_analysis.deploy_running_concurrently_with_a_launc: Hazard: launch reads the stamp during a deploy that is mid-rsync. Mitigation: rsync writes to dest paths atomically (rsync uses temp file + rename per file), and the stamp is written LAST via mv-into-place. Worst case: launch sees the OLD stamp matching the NEW files (race window where some files are new but stamp not yet rewritten) — would falsely flag drift. This is acceptable because the operator just ran deploy intentionally; a single false-positive on the next launch is a minor annoyance. To eliminate even that: deploy-to-usrlib.sh acquires an flock on /tmp/rednote-mcp-deploy.lock for the entire script. Launch-time check optionally acquires a SHARED flock on the same file (best-effort, non-blocking) — if it fails to acquire, log 'deploy in progress, skipping drift check for this launch' and proceed. Recommended OPTIONAL extension; not required for v1.
ordering_hazard_analysis.package_json_version_bump_with_no_redepl: Hazard: developer bumps package.json version in source repo, commits, but does not run deploy-to-usrlib.sh. Source package.json is 0.2.5; installed package.json is still 0.2.4; stamp says 0.2.4. Launch reads installed package.json (0.2.4), compares to stamp (0.2.4), passes. Correct behavior: the check is about installed-vs-its-own-stamp, not source-vs-installed. The complementary 'source has moved past installed' check is the optional warning in step 9 of the launcher pseudocode (compare stamp.source_commit_sha against current source HEAD); WARN only, not gate.

issues.title: arch-prop-3 — npm preinstall guard: hook is `preinstall`; lives in BOTH source and deployed package.json (rsync handles propagation); deploy script does NOT trigger npm install so the guard never fires during sanctioned deploy
issues.description: The guard is a 4-line addition to package.json scripts. Hook choice is `preinstall` because it is the FIRST script npm runs, before any tarball extraction or dependency resolution — so it can refuse before npm has done anything destructive. It must be in BOTH the source repo's package.json AND the deployed copy at /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json. Implementation surface and behavior PRESCRIBED below.
issues.location: PRIMARY: /root/rednote-mcp/package.json (scripts.preinstall added). PROPAGATES via deploy-to-usrlib.sh's rsync to /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json — but ONLY IF deploy-to-usrlib.sh's source/target are extended to include package.json (see below — it currently rsyncs dist/ only).
issues.runtime_evidence: Prior cycle proved the rednote-mcp package has 25 stealth fragments + a new tool that would all be wiped by `npm install -g rednote-mcp`. The 2026-04-04 happy-server incident is the precedent for what a global npm install does to a stealth-modified runtime.
issues.observation_notes: Concrete prescription in implementation_prescription field below.

rejected_alternatives.postinstall: Fires AFTER npm has already extracted the package and resolved dependencies. By the time postinstall runs, the damage (wiped dist/) is done. Postinstall would only be useful as a 'phone home' alarm, not a guard.
rejected_alternatives.prepublish: Fires only on `npm publish`, which we explicitly never want to allow against this fork in any case. prepublishOnly already exists for the build step. prepublish does not fire on `npm install`, so it does not block the wipe scenario.
rejected_alternatives.preinstall_AND_install: npm `install` script runs only when no preinstall script handles things. preinstall is sufficient and preferred.

npm_lifecycle_phases_blocked_by_preinsta: `npm install rednote-mcp`     (local install in some other project that depends on rednote-mcp)
`npm install` from inside /root/rednote-mcp without REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 (this is the EXPECTED dev workflow — see section below)
`npm pack` does NOT run preinstall (per npm docs, pack runs prepack only). So the deploy script can `npm pack` if it ever needs to without tripping the guard. Currently it doesn't.

`npm link` DOES run preinstall (per npm v7+ docs). This is desired — `npm link` against rednote-mcp would symlink /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp to the source dist/, but that bypasses the sha256 round-trip and is exactly what we want to forbid. Guard catches it.
explicit_npm_lifecycle_NOT_blocked_by_pr: `npm publish`        (would run prepublish, prepare, prepack, postpublish — not preinstall; we have prepublishOnly already; and we publish nothing from this fork anyway)
Direct execution of dist/cli.js by node      (this is the runtime path — nothing npm-related runs)

package_json_scripts_after_change.preinstall: node -e "if(process.env.REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK!=='1'){console.error('REFUSED: rednote-mcp must not be installed via npm. This fork has a stealth-modified dist/ that npm install would wipe. To deploy: run /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh from the source repo. See /root/rednote-mcp/MIGRATION-20260503.md and /root/rednote-mcp/CLAUDE.md.');process.exit(78);}"

exact_script_text.why_inline_node_one_liner_not_a_separate: A separate scripts/preinstall-guard.sh would not be present in the published tarball unless explicitly added to the files array; an inline `node -e` works in any context where node exists, which it does (the package's main is a node script). Inline is also visible in `npm view rednote-mcp scripts.preinstall` for an operator who is wondering why install fails. Node was chosen over bash for portability (npm contracts assume node).
exact_script_text.exit_code: 78 — same as arch-prop-2 (sysexits EX_CONFIG). Standardizes the rednote-mcp 'I refuse to do this configuration' signal across both gates.

default_rejection_message.literal_text: REFUSED: rednote-mcp must not be installed via npm. This fork has a stealth-modified dist/ that npm install would wipe. To deploy: run /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh from the source repo. See /root/rednote-mcp/MIGRATION-20260503.md and /root/rednote-mcp/CLAUDE.md.
default_rejection_message.destination: console.error → npm surfaces script stderr to the operator's terminal AND captures it in the npm log
default_rejection_message.operator_workflow_after_rejection: Operator reads message, navigates to /root/rednote-mcp, runs scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh. Done.

where_does_the_guard_live_source_or_depl.source_repo: /root/rednote-mcp/package.json — primary edit. This protects against `npm install -g /root/rednote-mcp` (operator pointing npm at the local repo) and `npm install` from any other project that has `"rednote-mcp": "file:/root/rednote-mcp"` as a dep.
where_does_the_guard_live_source_or_depl.deployed_copy: /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json — must propagate via deploy. This protects against `npm install -g rednote-mcp` (whether from the npm registry or from a local tarball) — the new tarball would replace the deployed package.json, but the OLD deployed package.json (which has the guard) gets a chance to run preinstall on the OLD copy first if the install is being run AS rednote-mcp's own scripts. NOTE: when npm installs a NEW version of a package, it runs the NEW version's preinstall, not the old one's. So the guard in the deployed package.json does NOT block an upstream-tarball install in the standard sense. What it DOES protect: local `npm rebuild` in /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp, and any operator who runs `cd /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp && npm install` (rebuilding deps in place).
where_does_the_guard_live_source_or_depl.important_corollary: The PRIMARY defense against `npm install -g rednote-mcp` from upstream is NOT the preinstall guard alone — it is the launch-time drift check (arch-prop-2) which detects the wiped dist/ on the next MCP start. The preinstall guard is one defense layer; arch-prop-2 is the second; the README banner is the third. Defense in depth.

applies_to_npm_link_npm_pack_npm_install.npm_install_g_rednote_mcp_from_registry: BLOCKED. The downloaded upstream tarball's package.json (0.2.3 from npm registry) does NOT contain our preinstall guard — the guard exists only in our fork's package.json. Therefore the FIRST install does not block. BUT: this exact scenario is what arch-prop-2's launch-time drift check catches. Arch-prop-3's job is to block the NEXT install (now that the rednote-mcp at /usr/lib/.../package.json has the guard, a subsequent `npm install -g` first runs the deployed package.json's preinstall — which refuses) AND to block any developer-side `npm install` from inside /root/rednote-mcp without the env var set.
applies_to_npm_link_npm_pack_npm_install.npm_install_g_from_local_repo_path: BLOCKED at the source side (the preinstall in /root/rednote-mcp/package.json fires immediately).
applies_to_npm_link_npm_pack_npm_install.npm_link: BLOCKED — npm v7+ runs preinstall during link.
applies_to_npm_link_npm_pack_npm_install.npm_pack: ALLOWED — pack only runs prepack. This is acceptable because pack alone does not modify any installed location; it just produces a .tgz file. If the operator then `npm install -g <that .tgz>`, the install of THAT tarball runs preinstall — which is the guard.
applies_to_npm_link_npm_pack_npm_install.npm_install_in_source_repo_for_dev_depen: EXPECTED workflow: developer in /root/rednote-mcp runs `npm install` to refresh node_modules. This would trip the guard. Resolution: the developer sets REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 for their interactive shell session (one-time `export REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1`), or prefixes the command (`REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install`). The deploy script does the same when it needs to (currently it does NOT — see next field). Document this in CLAUDE.md and the README banner. The friction is intentional: anyone running npm install must consciously assert 'I am authorizing this'.

deploy_script_interaction.implication: The existing deploy-to-usrlib.sh does NOT invoke npm install — it rsyncs dist/ only. Therefore the preinstall guard NEVER FIRES during sanctioned deploys. There is NO scenario where deploy-to-usrlib.sh needs to set REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 itself, because it never invokes any npm command that would trigger preinstall. This is good news: the guard is invisible to the sanctioned path.
what_DOES_need_to_change_in_deploy_scrip: 1. Extend rsync to also copy package.json from source to target. Currently the script only rsyncs dist/. Without this, the preinstall guard added to source package.json never reaches /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json.
2. Concretely: add a second rsync call OR extend the rsync set OR explicitly `cp /root/rednote-mcp/package.json /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json` after the dist/ rsync.
3. Extend step e (sha256 round-trip) to also verify package.json matches.

4. The .deploy-stamp from arch-prop-2 lists files in dist/ only — package.json sits one directory up. Decision: include /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json in arch-prop-2's check by computing its sha256 and storing it as a TOP-LEVEL field in the stamp (e.g. stamp.package_json_sha256), since stamp.files is dist/-relative.
deploy_script_interaction.what_does_NOT_need_to_change_in_deploy_s: The script does not need to set REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK because it does not call npm. If a future operator extends the deploy to do `npm rebuild` in the install path (e.g. for native deps), THAT step would need REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 — at which point the operator can `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm rebuild ...` inline.

ordering_hazard_analysis.fresh_host_bootstrap: Day 0 on a new host: /root/rednote-mcp does not exist; /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp does not exist. Operator needs to `git clone` source repo — that does not run npm. Operator then needs to `npm install` in source for dev deps (this is the FIRST trip on the guard — operator must `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install`). Then operator needs an installed copy at /usr/lib/.../rednote-mcp. One-time bootstrap: `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install -g /root/rednote-mcp/` (this trips both the source AND the target preinstall — both pass because the env var is set). Then deploy: scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh (rsync — no preinstall fired). Subsequent updates: edit dist/, run scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh, no npm involvement, no guard fired. CHICKEN-AND-EGG IS RESOLVED by the operator's one-time use of REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 during bootstrap, which is the SAME credential the deploy script uses (in spirit) — the operator is consciously asserting 'I authorize this install'.
ordering_hazard_analysis.developer_running_npm_install_for_dev_de: Trips the guard. Documented friction. Set the env var. See applies_to section above.
ordering_hazard_analysis.automation_running_npm_install: Trips the guard. INTENDED. If automation needs to run npm install, automation must set REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 explicitly — which is an audit point.
ordering_hazard_analysis.version_bump_workflow_with_npm_version: The npm version command runs `npm version` which internally runs scripts (preversion, version, postversion) — NOT preinstall. So `npm version patch` is unaffected. Safe.
ordering_hazard_analysis.yarn_pnpm_etc_users: Not applicable — this repo uses npm (per the lockfile evidence in dist deploy reports). If a future maintainer switches to yarn, the preinstall hook is honored by yarn too (yarn runs npm-style lifecycle scripts). pnpm v7+ also honors preinstall. No change needed.

issues.title: Cross-cutting: deploy-to-usrlib.sh must rsync package.json (not just dist/) for arch-prop-3 to actually propagate
issues.description: Today the deploy script's source and target are dist/ only. Arch-prop-3's preinstall guard is in package.json which lives ONE DIRECTORY UP from dist/. Without extending the deploy script to also propagate package.json, the guard added to /root/rednote-mcp/package.json never reaches /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/package.json — and the layered defense degrades to source-only enforcement. This is a one-line fix in deploy-to-usrlib.sh but it is mandatory for arch-prop-3 to be effective at the install path.
issues.location: /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh — extend SOURCE_DIR/TARGET_DIR or add a second rsync invocation for package.json (and probably README.md for the banner from arch-prop-3).
issues.runtime_evidence: ls /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/ shows package.json exists as a separate file at the same level as dist/. The deploy script's SOURCE_DIR and TARGET_DIR both end with /dist, so the parent's package.json is untouched.
issues.observation_notes: Two implementation options. Option A: change the deploy script's defaults to rsync the package root (excluding node_modules, .git, .archive, src/) — simpler, broader, propagates README.md and any future top-level docs automatically. Option B: keep dist/ rsync and add explicit `cp /root/rednote-mcp/{package.json,README.md} /usr/lib/node_modules/rednote-mcp/` at the end. Recommend Option A with --exclude flags, because it composes naturally with arch-prop-2's package.json hash check: any future top-level file (e.g. a CHANGELOG.md) auto-propagates without re-editing the deploy script.

exact_diff_to_deploy_script: AND:    Update step a's `find` pattern to scope syntax-checking to dist/ only: `find $SOURCE_DIR/dist -type f -name '*.js' -print0` instead of `find $SOURCE_DIR -type f -name '*.js' -print0` — node --check is for runtime js, not for the various tooling .js files that may live above dist/.
AND:    Update step b/d sha256 calculation to scope to dist/+package.json+README.md (or, simpler: scope to whatever rsync actually copied — `find $TARGET_DIR -type f -not -path '*/node_modules/*'`).

exclusion_list_rationale.node_modules: Massive (300+ packages, hundreds of MB). Already installed in the right places by `npm install` in the source repo. Should not be force-pushed to the install path; the install path has its own node_modules tree.
exclusion_list_rationale..git: Git metadata is source-only. Never deploy.
exclusion_list_rationale.src: TypeScript sources are pre-compiled to dist/; the install path needs only the compiled artifacts.
exclusion_list_rationale.tests: Per the existing files array in package.json, tests are not part of the published artifact.
exclusion_list_rationale.jest_config_tsconfig_gitignore: Build/test config files; not part of runtime.

summary.runtime_health_rationale: Same as prior cycle: the source-of-truth invariant is now fixed (deploy script exists, MIGRATION-20260503.md documents it, CLAUDE.md operator note exists), but the two layered defenses against recurrence (launch-time drift check, npm preinstall guard) remain unbuilt. Until built, the system is one operator shortcut away from re-incident.
clean_areas: Deploy script is well-structured: explicit step labeling (a/b/c/d/e), node --check gate, rsync --checksum --delete, sha256 round-trip, clear exit codes. The proposed extensions (step f stamp writer, broader rsync scope) compose cleanly onto its existing structure.
package.json is small and well-organized; adding a single preinstall key is a 1-line surface change.
cli.js has a clear pre-mode-split section (lines 1-176) where the launch-time check naturally lives — no awkward refactor required.

answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_2_check_lives_where: INSIDE dist/cli.js, called as a synchronous helper before any McpServer construction. NOT a wrapper script around `node /usr/lib/.../cli.js`. Reason: there is no existing wrapper; adding one moves the integrity gate outside /root/rednote-mcp where it cannot be audited by the source-of-truth invariant.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_2_stamp_contents: JSON file with: schema_version, deployed_at, deployed_by, source_path, source_commit_sha, source_commit_dirty, package_version, files{relpath: sha256}, files_count, manifest_sha256. The files map is the gating field; everything else is forensic context.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_2_failure_mode: HARD-FAIL with exit 78 (EX_CONFIG). Multi-line stderr message listing each mismatched file. NOT warn-and-continue — the 2026-04-04 precedent requires loud failure over silent degradation. All output to stderr (stdio mode would corrupt MCP frames otherwise).
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_2_stamp_writer: deploy-to-usrlib.sh — extend with a step f after the existing step e (sha256 round-trip), atomic-mv-into-place to avoid race with concurrent launches.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_3_lifecycle_hook: preinstall (not prepublish, not postinstall — those don't block early enough or don't fire during install).
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_3_error_message_and_exit_code: Literal message: 'REFUSED: rednote-mcp must not be installed via npm. This fork has a stealth-modified dist/ that npm install would wipe. To deploy: run /root/rednote-mcp/scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh from the source repo. See /root/rednote-mcp/MIGRATION-20260503.md and /root/rednote-mcp/CLAUDE.md.' Exit code 78 (EX_CONFIG) — same convention as arch-prop-2.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_3_npm_link_pack_install_g: preinstall blocks: install (local + global), link, ci. preinstall does NOT block: pack, publish, version. Pack producing a .tgz is harmless because the .tgz's eventual install would itself trip preinstall. Publish is irrelevant for this fork.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.arch_prop_3_in_source_or_deployed_packag: BOTH. Source guards the dev workflow (`npm install` in /root/rednote-mcp must be `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install`). Deployed guards `npm rebuild` in /usr/lib/.../ and any local re-install. The PRIMARY defense against an upstream `npm install -g rednote-mcp` is arch-prop-2's launch-time check, not arch-prop-3 alone (the upstream tarball does not contain our guard).
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.cross_cutting_existing_deploy_script_han: It does not need to handle it as a script — the deploy script does NOT invoke npm install, so preinstall NEVER FIRES during sanctioned deploys. What the deploy script DOES need to do: rsync package.json to the install path so the deployed copy gains the guard. This is one rsync-flag change (raise SOURCE_DIR/TARGET_DIR one level + add --exclude flags). See arch-cross-cutting-1.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.cross_cutting_ordering_hazards: Three identified, all resolvable: (1) First-launch-with-no-stamp: resolved by mandating `scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh` as part of fresh-host bootstrap (T0'-5 in MIGRATION-20260503.md already says this; the new check makes the requirement enforceable instead of advisory). (2) Stamp predates check module: not actually a hazard — the first deploy that ships the check module also writes the stamp listing the check module; subsequent launches pass cleanly. (3) Concurrent deploy + launch: rare race window where launch sees old stamp + new files. Mitigated by atomic stamp mv + (optional v2) flock around the deploy.
answers_to_orchestrator_questions.cross_cutting_bootstrap_problem: Yes — fresh host needs ONE-TIME `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install` in source repo to get dev deps, then `REDNOTE_DEPLOY_OK=1 npm install -g /root/rednote-mcp/` (or equivalent — operator chooses) to seed /usr/lib/.../rednote-mcp, then `scripts/deploy-to-usrlib.sh` writes the stamp. From that point forward: edit dist/, run deploy script, no npm involvement. Bootstrap is documented in the README banner from arch-prop-3 and updated MIGRATION-20260503.md T0'-5.
